answer_text:
Let

\[
g(x)=x^{3}+4x^{2}+5x+6,\qquad h(x)=2x^{3}+7x^{2}+9x+10.
\]

Since \(f(x)=x^{2}+ax+b\) is a common quadratic factor, it must be the gcd of \(g\) and \(h\).

Compute:

\[
h(x)-2g(x)=\left(2x^{3}+7x^{2}+9x+10\right)-\left(2x^{3}+8x^{2}+10x+12\right)
\]

\[
=-x^{2}-x-2.
\]

Thus the common quadratic factor is

\[
f(x)=x^{2}+x+2.
\]

Check:

\[
x^{3}+4x^{2}+5x+6=(x+3)(x^{2}+x+2),
\]

\[
2x^{3}+7x^{2}+9x+10=(2x+5)(x^{2}+x+2).
\]

So

\[
f(P)=P^{2}+P+2.
\]

Therefore, as written,

\[
\boxed{Q=P^{2}+P+2\text{ (so if }P=1,\ Q=4\text{)}}.
\]
